description:
Substrate role-file debloat + reliability architecture. Designed in POLYBIUS<->PRINCIPAL session 2026-05-22.

PROBLEM: substrate role files bloated via an accretion ratchet (every observed failure -> a new documented discipline + provenance, nothing ever removed). Current sizes: operating-disciplines.md 2110 lines, MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md 1299, MAJOR_PLINY.md 801, CAPTAIN_DAEDALUS.md 633.

THESIS: line count is a proxy, not the disease. The real test is ADHERENCE, not completeness. Past a threshold, more always-loaded instruction (a) taxes every turn in tokens, (b) DEGRADES adherence to the load-bearing rules (signal dilution / lost-in-the-middle), (c) accretes drift + contradiction (MAJOR_POLYBIUS 7.3 and MAJOR_PLINY 6.1 had silently diverged). So ~2000 always-loaded lines is too many - because most of it is duplication + provenance prose + conditional procedures that need not be ambient.

SOLUTION (two new layers move reliability OUT of memorized-instruction):
- COMPOSITION layer: instructions become a composable module library; the orchestrator selects per task and delivers via channels every agent already has (dispatch prompt / disk module via Read / bw via Bash). No Skill-tool grant needed.
- ENFORCEMENT layer: harness-owned triggers (hooks + cron) carry self-contained instructions at the moment of action; a checker agent backstops judgment items. Adherence becomes PreToolUse-gated + Stop/PostToolUse-reminded + peer-checked, not memorized.

Together these make cutting the role files SAFE: operational core stays small and crisp; reference loads on demand; provenance is archived in bw and cited, never inlined.

CHILD MAP (in creation order): 1 = decision (CLI not MCP); 2 = findings (skill-grant/caching/no-real-agent-tests); 3 = method (3-bucket + 3-tier); 4 = composition layer; 5 = enforcement layer; 6 = first execution (POLYBIUS pass).
title: Substrate role-file debloat + reliability architecture
